title: Hooray for the sockets interface | APNIC Blog
excerpt: In 1983, BSD 4.2 introduced sockets, treating network communication like file I/O. This simplification sped UNIX adoption of shared protocols and services, marking a key turning point in modern networking.
content_html:
Generated with AI.

In 1983, the University of California, Berkeley campus (UCB) released version 4.2 of its UNIX operating system, the Berkeley Standard Distribution (BSD). For many people, this is the ‘epoch event’ that defines the birth of online services, because it is the version that released the BSD ‘sockets’ model of networking into the world. In effect, the ‘right place, right time’ combined for computing systems and an operating system to run on them. This led to a massive increase in access to network services worldwide.

The installation of this first ubiquitous network approach was by tape, which you got in the mail.

To modern eyes, this may seem strange, given that modern operating system installation is most often a network-driven event. If you do not download a full ISO image or bootable VMDK disk image from the network, you tend to download a smaller system that bootstraps from the network. This is normal — the network is assumed.

Back in the 1980s, while ‘a network’ might exist, it was both too narrow — dial-up telephone at speeds as low as 1200 or 2400 baud — and lacked common protocols to specify how to find and fetch content. Even if you had access to ‘the network’, it was difficult to reliably retrieve something like the binary code of a new operating system. It looked different almost everywhere.

Sockets are a large part of the story that changed this. After sockets, networked UNIX systems began to look broadly consistent. We arrived at a more standardized model of network access.

Prior versions of BSD for PDP-11 minicomputers, dating back to 1978, had been released to the research community worldwide on tape: 30 copies of the code for version 1, and 75 copies for version 2. The system was released under a licence issued on behalf of ‘the Regents of the University of California’, and it carefully limited liability and user rights. You received the code in the post on a reel of tape.

If you wanted to update your code, the Regents required continuity of the people signing the licences. This caused problems, as academic roles often shifted between department members in ways the Regents’ lawyers did not anticipate.

When you received an operating system like this on tape, it consisted of a linear series of recordings. Each was denoted by an ‘End of Transmission’ (EOT) marker, which you could skip to reach the next block. In effect, a stream of bytes was read in a fixed format.

To begin, you were provided with minimal hex code to enter by hand at a switch console. This depended on your computer architecture. The code bootstrapped by reading the first tape block into memory, after which you jumped into memory to run it as a bootstrap loader.

Entering the hex meant setting switches across a 16-bit field — up or down, on or off — checking them against a printed listing, and then committing them to memory one address at a time. It was slow and error-prone. The true end-of-tape marker was a silver label that triggered a photoelectric diode to stop the tape motor.

After loading the bootstrap loader, you could format a disk and unpack tape archive (TAR) data from the tape onto it. This encoded all operating system files onto the local disk. The process took most of a day. If you needed to recompile the system, for example, to add device drivers, it could take two or three days. Despite this, many people accepted the cost to gain access to a UNIX system.

Version 4.2BSD shipped with several significant changes. These included bug fixes, an improved filesystem quota method, and symbolic links — which initially puzzled users accustomed to hard links. Alongside these was the Berkeley sockets networking system, developed under contract from the Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA). At the time, it wasn’t clear how significant this was.

Before sockets

Before this, access to network services on UNIX relied on programs such as cu or tip. These acted as terminal emulators, sending characters over serial ports to modems. Many early modems were acoustic couplers attached to telephone handsets using Velcro — one part was a microphone, the other a speaker. You connected by dialling the phone.

Tools like the Unix-to-Unix Copy Program (UUCP) used scripts that called cu or similar tools to establish connections, then transferred data. Even using cu was slow. Terminal types in tools such as the vi editor (a BSD innovation by Bill Joy, later a co-founder of Sun Microsystems) reduced screen updates to suit slow links.

UUCP was how we sent mail, read network news, and received (small) files. For much of the research community, it effectively was the network. Others used IBM BITNET or systems such as the UK Science and Engineering Research Council Network (SERC), later JANET (Joint Academic Network), which operated over X.25 data networks.

Sockets and the UNIX file model

Sockets changed all this. They provided a simple, consistent way to connect to ARPANET systems. Crucially, they reused an existing UNIX abstraction — the file descriptor. In simple terms, a socket behaved like a file.

By adopting the UNIX file descriptor model, almost any program that wrote to a file or read a file could be converted to read and write to the network. Back-porting UUCP to work over ARPANET was not particularly hard, and convenient programs like FTP for file transfer, Telnet for online access, and a back-end for the SMTP mail system to talk to the UNIX Sendmail service (another feature of the BSD UNIX system) followed very rapidly. In a remarkably short space of time, almost everything that could talk to sockets had been written to talk to sockets, or some kind of shim program that talked to sockets for you.

Everything ‘just worked’. Or, in the case of the first release of 4.2BSD, it actually didn’t work.

Part of the problem was that most recipients of the 4.2BSD tape had no access to ARPANET. At the time, ARPANET was limited to a small group of US universities and research institutions, with only a few connections in Europe and Asia via satellite. Most sites lacked any network using ARPANET protocols. For example, the university I worked at had Ethernet, but most machines connected to it via serial links rather than directly. We were fortunate to have two Virtual Address Extension (VAX) systems on Ethernet, but one ran VAX/VMS and did not yet include the ARPANET networking code.

Sockets were ‘run’ by connecting them to UNIX-domain sockets, which resembled the existing pipe mechanism. Pipes behaved like special files; they appeared in the filesystem but contained no disk data, and reads depended on writes from another process. To test sockets, you could write C code that connected to one of these local pipes. However, the system was still buggy — our first attempt crashed UNIX. As shipped, the sockets library couldn’t actually communicate with anything.

From experiment to standard

Sockets were not the only candidate interface to the ARPANET protocols. AT&T Bell Labs was developing its own model for network I/O called ‘streams’, released as STREAMS (the capitalization apparently mattered, tied to AT&T’s growing inclination to patent or copyright anything with potential value). Like sockets, STREAMS presented an interface that closely resembled file I/O, making it highly approachable for C programmers already comfortable with working with files.

In practice, however, STREAMS was far less accessible. Its emergence coincided with a legal dispute between AT&T and BSD. As a result, the university regents became more cautious about distributing tapes, while AT&T itself grew increasingly wary of releasing its code to the wider world. Sockets, by contrast, had already arrived and were readily available.

Bill Joy’s new company, Sun Microsystems, soon exploded onto the market with a challenger to the VAX as the default computing platform, this time built around the Motorola 68000 CPU. These machines ran UNIX, specifically, BSD 4.2 and its successors, and so came with the sockets system available out of the box. Here was a desktop-class computer — a fast, high-resolution display, a full UNIX environment, Ethernet built in, and working sockets code from the moment it booted. What was not to love?

DEC responded in this market with the release of ULTRIX, built on progressively smaller VAX systems. ULTRIX drew heavily on BSD UNIX, or at least incorporated significant elements of it, and thus included sockets. One by one, major manufacturers abandoned their proprietary operating systems or introduced forms of UNIX compatibility, and in doing so acquired sockets code.

Even AT&T, while developing what became System V as a commercially ubiquitous version of UNIX, adopted sockets in its networking code. The marketplace of ideas had already decided; despite the appealing qualities of the streams model, networking meant sockets.

From that point on, progress came from many directions. Sun’s Network File System (NFS), built on UDP sockets, became widely adopted. At the same time, shim layers emerged to drive increasingly affordable Ethernet cards for IBM PCs, exposing socket abstractions to Windows environments. In effect, network protocol development settled around the TCP/IP and UDP/IP stack, accessed through sockets. Since then, large-scale innovation has mostly taken the form of refinement — improving performance, or adapting to IPv6 — until the arrival of QUIC, which reimagines session services over UDP and sidelines TCP. And yet, even QUIC ultimately writes to a UNIX socket.

Sockets took over the world.

sentences.en: Alongside these was the Berkeley sockets networking system, developed under contract from the Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA).
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有伯克利套接字网络系统，该系统是根据国防高级研究计划局 (DARPA) 的合同开发的。

sentences.en: At the time, it wasn’t clear how significant this was.
sentences.zh: 当时，还不清楚这有多重要。

blocks.html_en: Before sockets

sentences.en: Before sockets
sentences.zh: 插座之前

blocks.html_en: Before this, access to network services on UNIX relied on programs such as cu or tip. These acted as terminal emulators, sending characters over serial ports to modems. Many early modems were acoustic couplers attached to telephone handsets using Velcro — one part was a microphone, the other a speaker. You connected by dialling the phone.

sentences.en: Before this, access to network services on UNIX relied on programs such as cu or tip.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，UNIX上访问网络服务依赖于cu或tip等程序。

sentences.en: These acted as terminal emulators, sending characters over serial ports to modems.
sentences.zh: 它们充当终端仿真器，通过串行端口将字符发送到调制解调器。

sentences.en: Many early modems were acoustic couplers attached to telephone handsets using Velcro — one part was a microphone, the other a speaker.
sentences.zh: 许多早期的调制解调器都是声耦合器，使用尼龙搭扣连接到电话听筒上——一部分是麦克风，另一部分是扬声器。

sentences.en: You connected by dialling the phone.
sentences.zh: 您通过拨打电话进行连接。

blocks.html_en: Tools like the Unix-to-Unix Copy Program (UUCP) used scripts that called cu or similar tools to establish connections, then transferred data. Even using cu was slow. Terminal types in tools such as the vi editor (a BSD innovation by Bill Joy, later a co-founder of Sun Microsystems) reduced screen updates to suit slow links.

sentences.en: Tools like the Unix-to-Unix Copy Program (UUCP) used scripts that called cu or similar tools to establish connections, then transferred data.
sentences.zh: Unix 到 Unix 复制程序 (UUCP) 等工具使用调用 cu 的脚本或类似工具来建立连接，然后传输数据。

sentences.en: Even using cu was slow.
sentences.zh: 即使使用 cu 也很慢。

sentences.en: Terminal types in tools such as the vi editor (a BSD innovation by Bill Joy, later a co-founder of Sun Microsystems) reduced screen updates to suit slow links.
sentences.zh: vi 编辑器（Bill Joy 的 BSD 创新，后来成为 Sun Microsystems 的联合创始人）等工具中的终端类型减少了屏幕更新以适应慢速链接。

blocks.html_en: UUCP was how we sent mail, read network news, and received (small) files. For much of the research community, it effectively was the network. Others used IBM BITNET or systems such as the UK Science and Engineering Research Council Network (SERC), later JANET (Joint Academic Network), which operated over X.25 data networks.

sentences.en: UUCP was how we sent mail, read network news, and received (small) files.
sentences.zh: UUCP 是我们发送邮件、阅读网络新闻和接收（小）文件的方式。

sentences.en: For much of the research community, it effectively was the network.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数研究界来说，它实际上就是网络。

sentences.en: Others used IBM BITNET or systems such as the UK Science and Engineering Research Council Network (SERC), later JANET (Joint Academic Network), which operated over X.25 data networks.
sentences.zh: 其他人则使用 IBM BITNET 或英国科学与工程研究委员会网络 (SERC) 等系统，以及后来的 JANET（联合学术网络），它们通过 X.25 数据网络运行。

blocks.html_en: Sockets and the UNIX file model

sentences.en: Sockets and the UNIX file model
sentences.zh: 套接字和 UNIX 文件模型

blocks.html_en: Sockets changed all this. They provided a simple, consistent way to connect to ARPANET systems. Crucially, they reused an existing UNIX abstraction — the file descriptor. In simple terms, a socket behaved like a file.

sentences.en: Sockets changed all this.
sentences.zh: 套接字改变了这一切。

sentences.en: They provided a simple, consistent way to connect to ARPANET systems.
sentences.zh: 他们提供了一种简单、一致的方式来连接阿帕网系统。

sentences.en: Crucially, they reused an existing UNIX abstraction — the file descriptor.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，他们重用了现有的 UNIX 抽象——文件描述符。

sentences.en: In simple terms, a socket behaved like a file.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，套接字的行为就像文件一样。

blocks.html_en: By adopting the UNIX file descriptor model, almost any program that wrote to a file or read a file could be converted to read and write to the network. Back-porting UUCP to work over ARPANET was not particularly hard, and convenient programs like FTP for file transfer, Telnet for online access, and a back-end for the SMTP mail system to talk to the UNIX Sendmail service (another feature of the BSD UNIX system) followed very rapidly. In a remarkably short space of time, almost everything that could talk to sockets had been written to talk to sockets, or some kind of shim program that talked to sockets for you.

sentences.en: By adopting the UNIX file descriptor model, almost any program that wrote to a file or read a file could be converted to read and write to the network.
sentences.zh: 通过采用 UNIX 文件描述符模型，几乎任何写入文件或读取文件的程序都可以转换为读取和写入网络。

sentences.en: Back-porting UUCP to work over ARPANET was not particularly hard, and convenient programs like FTP for file transfer, Telnet for online access, and a back-end for the SMTP mail system to talk to the UNIX Sendmail service (another feature of the BSD UNIX system) followed very rapidly.
sentences.zh: 将 UUCP 向后移植到 ARPANET 上工作并不是特别困难，随后很快就出现了方便的程序，例如用于文件传输的 FTP、用于在线访问的 Telnet 以及用于 SMTP 邮件系统与 UNIX Sendmail 服务（BSD UNIX 系统的另一个功能）对话的后端。

sentences.en: In a remarkably short space of time, almost everything that could talk to sockets had been written to talk to sockets, or some kind of shim program that talked to sockets for you.
sentences.zh: 在非常短的时间内，几乎所有可以与套接字通信的东西都被编写为与套接字通信，或者某种为您与套接字通信的填充程序。

blocks.html_en: Everything ‘just worked’. Or, in the case of the first release of 4.2BSD, it actually didn’t work.

sentences.en: Everything ‘just worked’.
sentences.zh: 一切都“正常”。

sentences.en: Or, in the case of the first release of 4.2BSD, it actually didn’t work.
sentences.zh: 或者，在 4.2BSD 的第一个版本中，它实际上不起作用。

blocks.html_en: Part of the problem was that most recipients of the 4.2BSD tape had no access to ARPANET. At the time, ARPANET was limited to a small group of US universities and research institutions, with only a few connections in Europe and Asia via satellite. Most sites lacked any network using ARPANET protocols. For example, the university I worked at had Ethernet, but most machines connected to it via serial links rather than directly. We were fortunate to have two Virtual Address Extension (VAX) systems on Ethernet, but one ran VAX/VMS and did not yet include the ARPANET networking code.

sentences.en: Part of the problem was that most recipients of the 4.2BSD tape had no access to ARPANET.
sentences.zh: 部分问题在于 4.2BSD 磁带的大多数接收者无法访问阿帕网。

sentences.en: At the time, ARPANET was limited to a small group of US universities and research institutions, with only a few connections in Europe and Asia via satellite.
sentences.zh: 当时，阿帕网仅限于一小部分美国大学和研究机构，在欧洲和亚洲只有少数通过卫星连接。

sentences.en: Most sites lacked any network using ARPANET protocols.
sentences.zh: 大多数站点缺乏使用阿帕网协议的网络。

sentences.en: For example, the university I worked at had Ethernet, but most machines connected to it via serial links rather than directly.
sentences.zh: 例如，我工作的大学有以太网，但大多数机器通过串行链路而不是直接连接到它。

sentences.en: We were fortunate to have two Virtual Address Extension (VAX) systems on Ethernet, but one ran VAX/VMS and did not yet include the ARPANET networking code.
sentences.zh: 我们很幸运在以太网上拥有两个虚拟地址扩展 (VAX) 系统，但其中一个运行 VAX/VMS，但尚未包含 ARPANET 网络代码。

blocks.html_en: Sockets were ‘run’ by connecting them to UNIX-domain sockets, which resembled the existing pipe mechanism. Pipes behaved like special files; they appeared in the filesystem but contained no disk data, and reads depended on writes from another process. To test sockets, you could write C code that connected to one of these local pipes. However, the system was still buggy — our first attempt crashed UNIX. As shipped, the sockets library couldn’t actually communicate with anything.

sentences.en: Sockets were ‘run’ by connecting them to UNIX-domain sockets, which resembled the existing pipe mechanism.
sentences.zh: 套接字通过将它们连接到 UNIX 域套接字来“运行”，这类似于现有的管道机制。

sentences.en: Pipes behaved like special files; they appeared in the filesystem but contained no disk data, and reads depended on writes from another process.
sentences.zh: 管道的行为就像特殊文件一样；它们出现在文件系统中，但不包含磁盘数据，并且读取依赖于另一个进程的写入。

sentences.en: To test sockets, you could write C code that connected to one of these local pipes.
sentences.zh: 要测试套接字，您可以编写连接到这些本地管道之一的 C 代码。

sentences.en: However, the system was still buggy — our first attempt crashed UNIX.
sentences.zh: 然而，系统仍然存在缺陷——我们的第一次尝试使 UNIX 崩溃了。

sentences.en: As shipped, the sockets library couldn’t actually communicate with anything.
sentences.zh: 在交付时，套接字库实际上无法与任何东西通信。

blocks.html_en: From experiment to standard

sentences.en: From experiment to standard
sentences.zh: 从实验到标准

blocks.html_en: Sockets were not the only candidate interface to the ARPANET protocols. AT&T Bell Labs was developing its own model for network I/O called ‘streams’, released as STREAMS (the capitalization apparently mattered, tied to AT&T’s growing inclination to patent or copyright anything with potential value). Like sockets, STREAMS presented an interface that closely resembled file I/O, making it highly approachable for C programmers already comfortable with working with files.

sentences.en: Sockets were not the only candidate interface to the ARPANET protocols.
sentences.zh: 套接字并不是阿帕网协议的唯一候选接口。

sentences.en: AT&T Bell Labs was developing its own model for network I/O called ‘streams’, released as STREAMS (the capitalization apparently mattered, tied to AT&T’s growing inclination to patent or copyright anything with potential value).
sentences.zh: AT&T 贝尔实验室正在开发自己的网络 I/O 模型，称为“流”，以 STREAMS 的形式发布（大小写显然很重要，这与 AT&T 对任何具有潜在价值的事物越来越倾向于专利或版权相关）。

sentences.en: Like sockets, STREAMS presented an interface that closely resembled file I/O, making it highly approachable for C programmers already comfortable with working with files.
sentences.zh: 与套接字一样，STREAMS 提供了一个与文件 I/O 非常相似的接口，这对于已经习惯使用文件的 C 程序员来说非常容易上手。

blocks.html_en: In practice, however, STREAMS was far less accessible. Its emergence coincided with a legal dispute between AT&T and BSD. As a result, the university regents became more cautious about distributing tapes, while AT&T itself grew increasingly wary of releasing its code to the wider world. Sockets, by contrast, had already arrived and were readily available.

sentences.en: In practice, however, STREAMS was far less accessible.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，STREAMS 的访问性要差得多。

sentences.en: Its emergence coincided with a legal dispute between AT&T and BSD.
sentences.zh: 它的出现恰逢 AT&T 和 BSD 之间的法律纠纷。

sentences.en: As a result, the university regents became more cautious about distributing tapes, while AT&T itself grew increasingly wary of releasing its code to the wider world.
sentences.zh: 结果，大学董事会对于分发磁带变得更加谨慎，而 AT&T 本身对于向更广阔的世界发布其代码也变得越来越谨慎。

sentences.en: Sockets, by contrast, had already arrived and were readily available.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，插座已经到货并且随时可用。

blocks.html_en: Bill Joy’s new company, Sun Microsystems, soon exploded onto the market with a challenger to the VAX as the default computing platform, this time built around the Motorola 68000 CPU. These machines ran UNIX, specifically, BSD 4.2 and its successors, and so came with the sockets system available out of the box. Here was a desktop-class computer — a fast, high-resolution display, a full UNIX environment, Ethernet built in, and working sockets code from the moment it booted. What was not to love?

sentences.en: Bill Joy’s new company, Sun Microsystems, soon exploded onto the market with a challenger to the VAX as the default computing platform, this time built around the Motorola 68000 CPU.
sentences.zh: Bill Joy 的新公司 Sun Microsystems 很快就在市场上大放异彩，它是 VAX 作为默认计算平台的挑战者，这次是围绕 Motorola 68000 CPU 构建的。

sentences.en: These machines ran UNIX, specifically, BSD 4.2 and its successors, and so came with the sockets system available out of the box.
sentences.zh: 这些机器运行 UNIX，特别是 BSD 4.2 及其后续版本，因此附带了开箱即用的套接字系统。

sentences.en: Here was a desktop-class computer — a fast, high-resolution display, a full UNIX environment, Ethernet built in, and working sockets code from the moment it booted.
sentences.zh: 这是一台桌面级计算机——快速、高分辨率的显示器、完整的 UNIX 环境、内置以太网以及从启动时起就可以工作的套接字代码。

sentences.en: What was not to love?
sentences.zh: 什么是不爱？

blocks.html_en: DEC responded in this market with the release of ULTRIX, built on progressively smaller VAX systems. ULTRIX drew heavily on BSD UNIX, or at least incorporated significant elements of it, and thus included sockets. One by one, major manufacturers abandoned their proprietary operating systems or introduced forms of UNIX compatibility, and in doing so acquired sockets code.

sentences.en: DEC responded in this market with the release of ULTRIX, built on progressively smaller VAX systems.
sentences.zh: DEC 在这一市场上做出了回应，发布了 ULTRIX，该产品基于逐渐小型化的 VAX 系统而构建。

sentences.en: ULTRIX drew heavily on BSD UNIX, or at least incorporated significant elements of it, and thus included sockets.
sentences.zh: ULTRIX 大量借鉴了 BSD UNIX，或者至少合并了它的重要元素，因此包含了套接字。

sentences.en: One by one, major manufacturers abandoned their proprietary operating systems or introduced forms of UNIX compatibility, and in doing so acquired sockets code.
sentences.zh: 主要制造商一一放弃了其专有操作系统或引入了 UNIX 兼容性形式，并在此过程中获得了套接字代码。

blocks.html_en: Even AT&T, while developing what became System V as a commercially ubiquitous version of UNIX, adopted sockets in its networking code. The marketplace of ideas had already decided; despite the appealing qualities of the streams model, networking meant sockets.

sentences.en: Even AT&T, while developing what became System V as a commercially ubiquitous version of UNIX, adopted sockets in its networking code.
sentences.zh: 甚至 AT&T 在开发 System V 作为商业上普遍使用的 UNIX 版本时，也在其网络代码中采用了套接字。

sentences.en: The marketplace of ideas had already decided; despite the appealing qualities of the streams model, networking meant sockets.
sentences.zh: 思想市场已经决定了；尽管流模型具有吸引人的品质，但网络意味着套接字。

blocks.html_en: From that point on, progress came from many directions. Sun’s Network File System (NFS), built on UDP sockets, became widely adopted. At the same time, shim layers emerged to drive increasingly affordable Ethernet cards for IBM PCs, exposing socket abstractions to Windows environments. In effect, network protocol development settled around the TCP/IP and UDP/IP stack, accessed through sockets. Since then, large-scale innovation has mostly taken the form of refinement — improving performance, or adapting to IPv6 — until the arrival of QUIC, which reimagines session services over UDP and sidelines TCP. And yet, even QUIC ultimately writes to a UNIX socket.

sentences.en: From that point on, progress came from many directions.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，进步来自多个方向。

sentences.en: Sun’s Network File System (NFS), built on UDP sockets, became widely adopted.
sentences.zh: Sun 的基于 UDP 套接字的网络文件系统 (NFS) 得到了广泛采用。

sentences.en: At the same time, shim layers emerged to drive increasingly affordable Ethernet cards for IBM PCs, exposing socket abstractions to Windows environments.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，填充层的出现推动了 IBM PC 以太网卡的价格越来越便宜，将套接字抽象暴露给 Windows 环境。

sentences.en: In effect, network protocol development settled around the TCP/IP and UDP/IP stack, accessed through sockets.
sentences.zh: 实际上，网络协议开发围绕 TCP/IP 和 UDP/IP 堆栈进行，通过套接字访问。

sentences.en: Since then, large-scale innovation has mostly taken the form of refinement — improving performance, or adapting to IPv6 — until the arrival of QUIC, which reimagines session services over UDP and sidelines TCP.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，大规模创新主要采取细化的形式——提高性能或适应 IPv6——直到 QUIC 的出现，它重新构想了基于 UDP 的会话服务并放弃了 TCP。

sentences.en: And yet, even QUIC ultimately writes to a UNIX socket.
sentences.zh: 然而，即使是 QUIC 最终也会写入 UNIX 套接字。

blocks.html_en: Sockets took over the world.

sentences.en: Sockets took over the world.
sentences.zh: 套接字接管了世界。

sentences.en: The views expressed by the authors of this blog are their own and do not necessarily reflect the views of APNIC.
sentences.zh: 本博客作者表达的观点仅代表他们自己的观点，并不一定反映 APNIC 的观点。

sentences.en: Please note a Code of Conduct applies to this blog.
sentences.zh: 请注意，行为准则适用于本博客。

content_html_zh:
用人工智能生成。

1983 年，加州大学伯克利分校 (UCB) 发布了 UNIX 操作系统 4.2 版，伯克利标准发行版 (BSD)。 对于许多人来说，这是定义在线服务诞生的“划时代事件”，因为它是向世界发布 BSD“套接字”网络模型的版本。 实际上，“正确的地点、正确的时间”结合了计算系统和在其上运行的操作系统。 这导致全球网络服务的访问量大幅增加。

第一个无处不在的网络方法的安装是通过磁带进行的，您可以通过邮件获得该磁带。

对于现代人来说，这可能看起来很奇怪，因为现代操作系统安装通常是网络驱动的事件。 如果您不从网络下载完整的 ISO 映像或可引导的 VMDK 磁盘映像，您往往会下载从网络引导的较小系统。 这是正常的——假设有网络。

早在 20 世纪 80 年代，虽然“网络”可能存在，但它的范围太窄——拨号电话的速度低至 1200 或 2400 波特——而且缺乏通用协议来指定如何查找和获取内容。 即使您可以访问“网络”，也很难可靠地检索新操作系统的二进制代码之类的东西。 几乎到处看起来都不一样。

套接字是改变这一情况的重要组成部分。 在套接字之后，网络 UNIX 系统开始看起来大体一致。 我们得出了一个更加标准化的网络访问模型。

PDP-11 小型机的 BSD 早期版本可追溯到 1978 年，已通过磁带向全球研究界发布：版本 1 的代码有 30 个副本，版本 2 的代码有 75 个副本。 该系统是根据代表“加州大学董事会”颁发的许可证发布的，并且它仔细地限制了责任和用户权利。 您在邮件中收到了一卷磁带上的代码。

如果您想更新代码，董事会需要签署许可证的人员保持连续性。 这引起了问题，因为学术角色经常在部门成员之间以摄政律师们没有预料到的方式转移。

当您收到这样的磁带操作系统时，它由一系列线性录音组成。 每个块都由“传输结束”(EOT) 标记表示，您可以跳过该标记到达下一个块。 实际上，字节流是以固定格式读取的。

首先，我们为您提供了最少的十六进制代码，以便您在交换机控制台上手动输入。 这取决于您的计算机体系结构。 通过将第一个磁带块读入内存来引导代码，然后跳入内存以将其作为引导加载程序运行。

输入十六进制意味着在 16 位字段中设置开关（向上或向下、打开或关闭），根据打印的列表检查它们，然后一次将它们提交到内存的一个地址。 它很慢而且容易出错。 真正的磁带末端标记是一个银色标签，它触发光电二极管来停止磁带电机。

加载引导加载程序后，您可以格式化磁盘并将磁带存档 (TAR) 数据从磁带解压到磁盘上。 这会将所有操作系统文件编码到本地磁盘上。 这个过程花了大半天的时间。 如果您需要重新编译系统，例如添加设备驱动程序，可能需要两到三天的时间。 尽管如此，许多人还是接受了访问 UNIX 系统的成本。

4.2BSD 版本附带了几项重大更改。 其中包括错误修复、改进的文件系统配额方法和符号链接——这最初让习惯硬链接的用户感到困惑。 除此之外，还有伯克利套接字网络系统，该系统是根据国防高级研究计划局 (DARPA) 的合同开发的。 当时，还不清楚这有多重要。

插座之前

在此之前，UNIX上访问网络服务依赖于cu或tip等程序。 它们充当终端仿真器，通过串行端口将字符发送到调制解调器。 许多早期的调制解调器都是声耦合器，使用尼龙搭扣连接到电话听筒上——一部分是麦克风，另一部分是扬声器。 您通过拨打电话进行连接。

Unix 到 Unix 复制程序 (UUCP) 等工具使用调用 cu 的脚本或类似工具来建立连接，然后传输数据。 即使使用 cu 也很慢。 vi 编辑器（Bill Joy 的 BSD 创新，后来成为 Sun Microsystems 的联合创始人）等工具中的终端类型减少了屏幕更新以适应慢速链接。

UUCP 是我们发送邮件、阅读网络新闻和接收（小）文件的方式。 对于大多数研究界来说，它实际上就是网络。 其他人则使用 IBM BITNET 或英国科学与工程研究委员会网络 (SERC) 等系统，以及后来的 JANET（联合学术网络），它们通过 X.25 数据网络运行。

套接字和 UNIX 文件模型

套接字改变了这一切。 他们提供了一种简单、一致的方式来连接阿帕网系统。 至关重要的是，他们重用了现有的 UNIX 抽象——文件描述符。 简单来说，套接字的行为就像文件一样。

通过采用 UNIX 文件描述符模型，几乎任何写入文件或读取文件的程序都可以转换为读取和写入网络。 将 UUCP 向后移植到 ARPANET 上工作并不是特别困难，随后很快就出现了方便的程序，例如用于文件传输的 FTP、用于在线访问的 Telnet 以及用于 SMTP 邮件系统与 UNIX Sendmail 服务（BSD UNIX 系统的另一个功能）对话的后端。 在非常短的时间内，几乎所有可以与套接字通信的东西都被编写为与套接字通信，或者某种为您与套接字通信的填充程序。

一切都“正常”。 或者，在 4.2BSD 的第一个版本中，它实际上不起作用。

部分问题在于 4.2BSD 磁带的大多数接收者无法访问阿帕网。 当时，阿帕网仅限于一小部分美国大学和研究机构，在欧洲和亚洲只有少数通过卫星连接。 大多数站点缺乏使用阿帕网协议的网络。 例如，我工作的大学有以太网，但大多数机器通过串行链路而不是直接连接到它。 我们很幸运在以太网上拥有两个虚拟地址扩展 (VAX) 系统，但其中一个运行 VAX/VMS，但尚未包含 ARPANET 网络代码。

套接字通过将它们连接到 UNIX 域套接字来“运行”，这类似于现有的管道机制。 管道的行为就像特殊文件一样；它们出现在文件系统中，但不包含磁盘数据，并且读取依赖于另一个进程的写入。 要测试套接字，您可以编写连接到这些本地管道之一的 C 代码。 然而，系统仍然存在缺陷——我们的第一次尝试使 UNIX 崩溃了。 在交付时，套接字库实际上无法与任何东西通信。

从实验到标准

套接字并不是阿帕网协议的唯一候选接口。 AT&T 贝尔实验室正在开发自己的网络 I/O 模型，称为“流”，以 STREAMS 的形式发布（大小写显然很重要，这与 AT&T 对任何具有潜在价值的事物越来越倾向于专利或版权相关）。 与套接字一样，STREAMS 提供了一个与文件 I/O 非常相似的接口，这对于已经习惯使用文件的 C 程序员来说非常容易上手。

但实际上，STREAMS 的访问性要差得多。 它的出现恰逢 AT&T 和 BSD 之间的法律纠纷。 结果，大学董事会对于分发磁带变得更加谨慎，而 AT&T 本身对于向更广阔的世界发布其代码也变得越来越谨慎。 相比之下，插座已经到货并且随时可用。

Bill Joy 的新公司 Sun Microsystems 很快就在市场上大放异彩，它是 VAX 作为默认计算平台的挑战者，这次是围绕 Motorola 68000 CPU 构建的。 这些机器运行 UNIX，特别是 BSD 4.2 及其后续版本，因此附带了开箱即用的套接字系统。 这是一台桌面级计算机——快速、高分辨率的显示器、完整的 UNIX 环境、内置以太网以及从启动时起就可以工作的套接字代码。 什么是不爱？

DEC 在这一市场上做出了回应，发布了 ULTRIX，该产品基于逐渐小型化的 VAX 系统而构建。 ULTRIX 大量借鉴了 BSD UNIX，或者至少合并了它的重要元素，因此包含了套接字。 主要制造商一一放弃了其专有操作系统或引入了 UNIX 兼容性形式，并在此过程中获得了套接字代码。

甚至 AT&T 在开发 System V 作为商业上普遍使用的 UNIX 版本时，也在其网络代码中采用了套接字。 思想市场已经决定了；尽管流模型具有吸引人的品质，但网络意味着套接字。

从那时起，进步来自多个方向。 Sun 的基于 UDP 套接字的网络文件系统 (NFS) 得到了广泛采用。 与此同时，填充层的出现推动了 IBM PC 以太网卡的价格越来越便宜，将套接字抽象暴露给 Windows 环境。 实际上，网络协议开发围绕 TCP/IP 和 UDP/IP 堆栈进行，通过套接字访问。 从那时起，大规模创新主要采取细化的形式——提高性能或适应 IPv6——直到 QUIC 的出现，它重新构想了基于 UDP 的会话服务并放弃了 TCP。 然而，即使是 QUIC 最终也会写入 UNIX 套接字。

套接字接管了世界。
